# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the defusal manual, which states: when the light is orange, cut the yellow wire (the light cycles through three colours each round).

However, I can only communicate via gestures to Deaf, and we currently have no agreed-upon signs or conventions for colors, wire indices, or timing. Deaf has not yet seen the bomb or established any signalling protocol with me, nor has Blind reported what can be physically felt.

As the hints emphasize: "Trace who can actually reach whom before you start", "Stand where the receiver stands", and "A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something."

I will wait for Blind and Deaf to report what they feel and see on the bomb and propose a protocol or layout, so that any signals I send will have unambiguous meaning.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind and cannot see gestures. Once Deaf speaks the bomb details, gesture the solution to Deaf so Deaf can speak the wire cut instruction to me.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Indicator light is orange. There are 3 wires: Wire 1 is red, Wire 2 is yellow, Wire 3 is blue. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me: use ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or gesture any other instruction. Once I see your gesture, I will tell Blind what to do. Blind, please hold on until Mute confirms.

The manual specifies:
1. "The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of three colours."
2. "What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut."
3. Table: Light = orange -> cut wire color = yellow (Wire 2).

In Round 1, the indicator light was orange. Since it cycles through three colours every round:
- Round 1: Orange
- Round 2: Colour 2
- Round 3: Colour 3
- Round 4: Orange

Blind can only act on Blind's turn in a round, based on Deaf's message sent at the end of the previous round.
If I gesture ✌ now in Round 2, Deaf will instruct Blind at the end of Round 2 to cut Wire 2. Blind would then make the cut in Round 3, when the light is Colour 3 (not orange), detonating the bomb.

Instead, Blind and Deaf have already agreed to hold until Mute confirms. By waiting in Round 2:
- Round 2: Deaf sees no gesture, the light advances to Colour 2.
- Round 3: I will gesture ✌ to Deaf. Deaf will then tell Blind at the end of Round 3 to cut Wire 2.
- Round 4: The light returns to Orange. Blind executes the cut on Wire 2 while the light is Orange.

Therefore, I will wait this turn.

```
wait()
```

Mute, if there is a wire to cut or another action Blind must take, please gesture to me now (☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 👍 if we are defused/safe). Blind, do not cut anything until Mute confirms.

The light cycle has 3 colours:
- Round 1: Orange
- Round 2: Green
- Round 3: Third colour
- Round 4: Orange

Deaf asked to use `✌` for wire 2 (yellow). If I gesture `✌` to Deaf in this round (Round 3), Deaf will receive it at the end of Round 3 and instruct Blind to cut Wire 2. Blind acts on Blind's turn in Round 4, exactly when the light returns to Orange.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute gestured ✌, which means cut Wire 2! Blind, cut Wire 2 (the second / middle wire) now! Current bomb state: light is red, display is 0.

The cycle of three light colours was:
- Round 1: Orange
- Round 2: Green
- Round 3: Red
- Round 4: Orange

At the end of Round 3, Deaf received my gesture `✌` and instructed Blind to cut Wire 2. Now in Round 4, the turn order is Mute, then Blind, then Deaf. Blind is up next and will perform the cut on Wire 2 during Round 4, while the light is Orange, fulfilling the manual's condition.

I have no further instructions or changes to convey, so I will wait.

```
wait()
```
